extraction_quality_notes: Ranking observations are limited to demographics, prior medical history, initial ED/ICU presentation facts, medication and ventilation exposures before ocular symptoms, and the day-3 ocular symptoms/exam/IOP available before ocular treatment.

The source provides no numeric heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, pH, PaCO2, lactate, bicarbonate, WBC count, CRP, renal function, temperature, chest imaging detail, or microbiology result.

The exact cessation time of bronchodilators relative to ocular symptom onset is approximate: aminophylline and noradrenaline were weaned within 24 h, and nebulised bronchodilators continued for a further day.
Right-eye counting-fingers visual acuity was kept as a qualitative severe visual-acuity impairment; left-eye 6/18 acuity was approximately converted to logMAR 0.48.

Several diagnosis-neutral suggested axis IDs were used where exact registry IDs were not found, including peripheral vascular disease history, critical care admission context, recent systemic corticosteroid exposure, inhaled anticholinergic exposure, right-eye pain, left-eye symptom involvement, ocular redness, right-eye counting-fingers acuity, corneal haze, and respiratory acidosis.
No expected-manifold label, final diagnosis field, paper-title-derived diagnosis, or ordinary disease-suffixed observed axis is included.
